claim: Ewing sarcoma family of tumors is a group of malignant small round blue cell tumors (SRBCTs) that affect children, adolescents, and young adults.
source: The Ewing sarcoma family of tumors is a group of malignant small round blue cell tumors (SRBCTs) that affect children, adolescents, and young adults.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Ewing sarcoma presented in the abstract.

claim: Ewing sarcoma tumors are characterized by reciprocal chromosomal translocations that generate chimeric fusion oncogenes.
source: The tumors are characterized by reciprocal chromosomal translocations that generate chimeric fusion oncogenes, the most common of which is EWSR1-FLI1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the molecular characteristics of Ewing sarcoma.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 is the most common fusion oncogene in Ewing sarcoma.
source: The tumors are characterized by reciprocal chromosomal translocations that generate chimeric fusion oncogenes, the most common of which is EWSR1-FLI1.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited in the manuscript.

claim: Survival is extremely poor for patients with metastatic or relapsed Ewing sarcoma.
source: Survival is extremely poor for patients with metastatic or relapsed disease, and no molecularly targeted therapy for this disease currently exists.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about Ewing sarcoma prognosis.

claim: No molecularly targeted therapy for Ewing sarcoma currently exists.
source: Survival is extremely poor for patients with metastatic or relapsed disease, and no molecularly targeted therapy for this disease currently exists.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of treatment options.

claim: The absence of a reliable genetic animal model of Ewing sarcoma has impaired investigation of tumor cell/microenvironmental interactions in vivo.
source: The absence of a reliable genetic animal model of Ewing sarcoma has impaired investigation of tumor cell/microenvironmental interactions in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations in the field based on the lack of appropriate models.

claim: A new genetic model of Ewing sarcoma based on Cre-inducible expression of human EWSR1-FLI1 in wild-type zebrafish causes rapid onset of SRBCTs at high penetrance.
source: We have developed a new genetic model of Ewing sarcoma based on Cre-inducible expression of human EWSR1-FLI1 in wild-type zebrafish, which causes rapid onset of SRBCTs at high penetrance.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing tumor development in zebrafish.

claim: Zebrafish tumors expressing EWSR1-FLI1 express canonical EWSR1-FLI1 target genes.
source: The tumors express canonical EWSR1-FLI1 target genes and stain for known Ewing sarcoma markers including CD99.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data and immunohistochemistry presented in the manuscript.

claim: Zebrafish tumors expressing EWSR1-FLI1 stain for CD99.
source: The tumors express canonical EWSR1-FLI1 target genes and stain for known Ewing sarcoma markers including CD99.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Growth of EWSR1-FLI1-driven tumors in zebrafish is associated with activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway.
source: Growth of tumors is associated with activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway, which we link to dysregulated extracellular matrix metabolism in general and heparan sulfate proteoglycan catabolism in particular.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining and western blot data showing pERK1/2 activation in tumors.

claim: MAPK/ERK pathway activation in EWSR1-FLI1-driven tumors is linked to dysregulated extracellular matrix metabolism.
source: Growth of tumors is associated with activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway, which we link to dysregulated extracellular matrix metabolism in general and heparan sulfate proteoglycan catabolism in particular.
evidence: This is supported by proteomic data showing upregulation of ECM-related proteins.

claim: MAPK/ERK pathway activation in EWSR1-FLI1-driven tumors is linked to dysregulated heparan sulfate proteoglycan catabolism.
source: Growth of tumors is associated with activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway, which we link to dysregulated extracellular matrix metabolism in general and heparan sulfate proteoglycan catabolism in particular.
evidence: This is supported by proteomic data showing upregulation of heparan sulfate catabolism enzymes.

claim: Surfen reduces ERK1/2 signaling in Ewing sarcoma cells.
source: Targeting heparan sulfate proteoglycans with the specific heparan sulfate antagonist Surfen reduces ERK1/2 signaling and decreases tumorigenicity of Ewing sarcoma cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data showing reduced pERK1/2 levels after surfen treatment.

claim: Surfen decreases tumorigenicity of Ewing sarcoma cells in vitro.
source: Targeting heparan sulfate proteoglycans with the specific heparan sulfate antagonist Surfen reduces ERK1/2 signaling and decreases tumorigenicity of Ewing sarcoma cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assays and colony formation assays shown in Figure 6.

claim: Surfen decreases tumorigenicity of Ewing sarcoma cells in vivo.
source: Targeting heparan sulfate proteoglycans with the specific heparan sulfate antagonist Surfen reduces ERK1/2 signaling and decreases tumorigenicity of Ewing sarcoma cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by zebrafish experiments showing reduced tumor growth with surfen treatment.

claim: Ewing sarcoma has a peak incidence in adolescents and young adults.
source: Ewing sarcoma is an aggressive sarcoma of bone and soft tissue with a peak incidence in adolescents and young adults (Gaspar et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established epidemiological knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Approximately 20-25% of Ewing sarcoma patients present with metastases at diagnosis.
source: Approximately 20–25% of patients present with metastases at diagnosis that are often resistant to intensive therapy (Gaspar et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Metastases in Ewing sarcoma are often resistant to intensive therapy.
source: Approximately 20–25% of patients present with metastases at diagnosis that are often resistant to intensive therapy (Gaspar et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 is found in 85% of Ewing sarcoma cases.
source: The most common oncofusion found in 85% of cases is EWSR1-FLI1 (Delattre et al., 1992; Grünewald et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established molecular knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Chimeric fusion oncoproteins in Ewing sarcoma act as aberrant transcription factors.
source: These chimeric fusion oncoproteins act as aberrant transcription factors deregulating hundreds of genes (e.g., genes involved in cell-cycle regulation, cell migration, and proliferation) by binding DNA enriched with GGAA motifs (Gangwal et al., 2008; Guillon et al., 2009; Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established molecular knowledge supported by citations.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 deregulates hundreds of genes by binding DNA enriched with GGAA motifs.
source: These chimeric fusion oncoproteins act as aberrant transcription factors deregulating hundreds of genes (e.g., genes involved in cell-cycle regulation, cell migration, and proliferation) by binding DNA enriched with GGAA motifs (Gangwal et al., 2008; Guillon et al., 2009; Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established molecular knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ERK1/2 activity is required for transformation of NIH-3T3 cells by EWSR1-FLI1.
source: ERK1/2 activity is required for transformation of NIH-3T3 cells by EWSR1-FLI1 (Silvany et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous research supported by citation.

claim: Combined expression of pAKT, pmTOR, and pERK predicted worse progression-free and overall survival in therapy-naive Ewing sarcoma samples.
source: In therapy-naive Ewing sarcoma samples, combined expression of pAKT, pmTOR, and pERK predicted worse progression-free and overall survival (van de Luijtgaarden et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Proteoglycans have essential roles in signal transduction and regulating cell adhesion, migration, and differentiation.
source: Proteoglycans are key molecular effectors of the cell surface and pericellular microenvironment with essential roles in signal transduction and regulating cell adhesion, migration, and differentiation.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about proteoglycan function.

claim: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans play an essential role in differentiation and migration of neural crest cells.
source: Importantly, heparan sulfate proteoglycans play an essential role in differentiation and migration of both neural crest and mesenchymal cells – both of them are considered as potential cell of origin of Ewing sarcoma (Henderson and Copp, 1997; Long and Huttner, 2019; Papy-Garcia and Albanese, 2017; Yaylaci et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans play an essential role in differentiation and migration of mesenchymal cells.
source: Importantly, heparan sulfate proteoglycans play an essential role in differentiation and migration of both neural crest and mesenchymal cells – both of them are considered as potential cell of origin of Ewing sarcoma (Henderson and Copp, 1997; Long and Huttner, 2019; Papy-Garcia and Albanese, 2017; Yaylaci et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Neural crest cells are considered as a potential cell of origin of Ewing sarcoma.
source: Importantly, heparan sulfate proteoglycans play an essential role in differentiation and migration of both neural crest and mesenchymal cells – both of them are considered as potential cell of origin of Ewing sarcoma (Henderson and Copp, 1997; Long and Huttner, 2019; Papy-Garcia and Albanese, 2017; Yaylaci et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about potential cell of origin supported by citations.

claim: Mesenchymal cells are considered as a potential cell of origin of Ewing sarcoma.
source: Importantly, heparan sulfate proteoglycans play an essential role in differentiation and migration of both neural crest and mesenchymal cells – both of them are considered as potential cell of origin of Ewing sarcoma (Henderson and Copp, 1997; Long and Huttner, 2019; Papy-Garcia and Albanese, 2017; Yaylaci et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about potential cell of origin supported by citations.

claim: Multiple attempts to create genetically engineered mouse models of Ewing sarcoma have not yielded a tractable model.
source: However, multiple attempts to create genetically engineered mouse models of Ewing sarcoma have not yielded a tractable model, likely due to the developmental toxicity of heterotopic expression of the oncofusion (Minas et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about previous modeling attempts supported by citation.

claim: The failure to create mouse models of Ewing sarcoma is likely due to the developmental toxicity of heterotopic expression of the oncofusion.
source: However, multiple attempts to create genetically engineered mouse models of Ewing sarcoma have not yielded a tractable model, likely due to the developmental toxicity of heterotopic expression of the oncofusion (Minas et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on previous research supported by citation.

claim: Transposon-mediated expression of human EWSR1-FLI1 drives SRBCT formation in zebrafish from 6 to 19 months of age.
source: Previously, we demonstrated that transposon-mediated expression of human EWSR1-FLI1 drives SRBCT formation in zebrafish from 6 to 19 months of age (Leacock et al., 2012).
evidence: This is data from previous research by the authors supported by citation.

claim: The previous zebrafish model of Ewing sarcoma had low penetrance and required tp53 deficiency.
source: While serving as proof of principle that EWSR1-FLI1 is tumorigenic in fish, the model had some limitations, including low penetrance, requirement for tp53 deficiency, and a low incidence of other tumor types such as leukemias.
evidence: This is data from previous research by the authors.

claim: 34% of eGFP-positive fish injected with ubi:RSG-EWSR1-FLI1 and Cre mRNA developed tumors.
source: We found that 34% of eGFP-positive fish developed tumors with onset during the first 3–4 weeks post-fertilization (Figure 1C) exhibiting SRBCT histology (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Tumors in the zebrafish model developed with onset during the first 3-4 weeks post-fertilization.
source: We found that 34% of eGFP-positive fish developed tumors with onset during the first 3–4 weeks post-fertilization (Figure 1C) exhibiting SRBCT histology (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: No tumors were observed in control groups (ubi:RSG-EWSR1-FLI1 with GFP RNA or uninjected).
source: No tumors were observed in either control group.
evidence: This is experimental data from the control groups.

claim: 58% of fish developing tumors had two or more tumors.
source: Among the fish developing tumors, 42% developed a single tumor, while 58% of fish had two or more tumors (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: 37% of EWSR1-FLI1-driven tumors in zebrafish were SRBCTs associated with the dorsal fin radial bones.
source: Thirty-seven percent of tumors were SRBCTs associated with the dorsal fin radial bones, while a further 15% of tumors arising from similar locations showed deep muscle invasiveness and were characterized as SRBCT with diffuse striated muscle infiltration.
evidence: This is experimental data from tumor location analysis.

claim: Zebrafish Ewing sarcoma tumor cells had nuclear localization of EWSR1-FLI1.
source: As expected, tumor cells had nuclear localization of EWSR1-FLI1, whereas control fish had no expression of FLI1 in the corresponding sites (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, top panel).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD99 is a cell surface glycoprotein that serves as a sensitive, clinically useful marker for Ewing sarcoma.
source: CD99 is a cell surface glycoprotein that serves as a sensitive, clinically useful marker for Ewing sarcoma (Muhammad et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Zebrafish Ewing sarcoma tumor cells express CD99 on the cell surface.
source: IHC confirmed the presence of CD99 on the cell surface of zebrafish Ewing sarcoma tumor cells (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Ewing sarcoma cells are characterized by the presence of glycogen and are positive for PAS staining.
source: Ewing sarcoma cells are characterized by the presence of the glycogen and are positive for Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining (Muhammad et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established histological knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Zebrafish tumors were positive for PAS staining.
source: Consistently, zebrafish tumors were positive for PAS staining (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is experimental data from PAS staining shown in Figure 2B.

claim: NR0B1 is a target of EWSR1-FLI1 that directly modulates transcription and oncogenesis in Ewing sarcoma.
source: NR0B1 is a target of EWSR1-FLI1 that directly modulates transcription and oncogenesis in Ewing sarcoma (Kinsey et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established molecular knowledge supported by citation.

claim: nr0b1 expression is upregulated in zebrafish tumor tissues compared to normal tissue.
source: Analysis of relative RNA expression showed upregulated expression of nr0b1 in tumor tissues compared to normal (Figure 2C), correlating with EWSR1-FLI1 expression level in tumor samples (N of repeats = 3, N of replicas = 3).
evidence: This is experimental data from qRT-PCR shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Ewing sarcoma cells exhibit cell-to-cell heterogeneity affecting proliferative and migratory potential of tumor cells.
source: Recently, it was shown that Ewing sarcoma cells exhibit cell-to-cell heterogeneity affecting proliferative and migratory potential of tumor cells (Franzetti et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous research supported by citation.

claim: Zebrafish tumor cells have varying levels of EWSR1-FLI1 expression.
source: Staining of zebrafish tumors showed that cells have varying levels of EWSR1-FLI1.
evidence: This is experimental data from immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The zebrafish model recapitulates the cell-to-cell heterogeneity found in human Ewing sarcoma cells.
source: Thus, the zebrafish model appears to recapitulate the cell-to-cell heterogeneity found in human Ewing sarcoma cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of varying EWSR1-FLI1 levels in zebrafish tumors.

claim: All zebrafish tumor samples expressed EWSR1-FLI1 on the protein level.
source: All tumor samples expressed EWSR1-FLI1 (Figure 2E) (N of repeats = 3, N of replicas = 3).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: 194 proteins were commonly upregulated in zebrafish tumors compared to control tissues.
source: We first identified a set of 194 proteins that were commonly upregulated in the zebrafish tumors compared to control tissues (p < 0.05).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis.

claim: Zebrafish tumor upregulated genes are enriched in human Ewing sarcoma dataset (NES = 1.501, FWER = 0.029).
source: GSEA showed enrichment of zebrafish tumor upregulated genes (NES = 1.501, FWER = 0.029) in the human Ewing sarcoma dataset but not in human rhabdomyosarcoma (NES = −1.476, FWER = 0.024) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is experimental data from GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Zebrafish tumor upregulated genes are not enriched in human rhabdomyosarcoma dataset (NES = -1.476, FWER = 0.024).
source: GSEA showed enrichment of zebrafish tumor upregulated genes (NES = 1.501, FWER = 0.029) in the human Ewing sarcoma dataset but not in human rhabdomyosarcoma (NES = −1.476, FWER = 0.024) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is experimental data from GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Proteins upregulated in human mesenchymal cells after EWSR1-FLI1 expression are significantly enriched in zebrafish tumors (NES: 1.540, FWER p value: 0.048).
source: We found that the list of proteins was significantly upregulated in zebrafish tumors (NES: 1.540, FWER p value: 0.048) confirming similarity between zebrafish and human disease (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is experimental data from GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Expression of EWSR1-FLI1 significantly increased embryonic mortality in zebrafish.
source: Expression of EWSR1-FLI1 significantly increased embryonic mortality in zebrafish (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is experimental data from survival analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Zebrafish expressing eGFP-2A-EWSR1-FLI1 under the ubi promoter have a distinct distribution pattern of eGFP-positive cells, predominantly on the fish dorsum, tail, and fins.
source: However, zebrafish expressing eGFP-2A-EWSR1-FLI1 under the ubi promoter have a distinct distribution pattern of eGFP-positive cells (Figure 3B, upper panel), predominantly on the fish dorsum, tail, and fins (Figure 3B, upper panel).
evidence: This is experimental data from imaging shown in Figure 3B.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 is efficiently expressed in zebrafish embryos on both the RNA and protein levels upon Cre-mediated recombination.
source: Upon Cre-mediated recombination, EWSR1-FLI is efficiently expressed in embryos on both the RNA and protein levels (Figure 3D, E).
evidence: This is experimental data from qRT-PCR and immunoblot shown in Figure 3D and 3E.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 drives the formation of outgrowths in embryonic model of the disease.
source: We also found that EWSR1-FLI1 drives the formation of outgrowths in embryonic model of the disease (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is experimental data from imaging shown in Figure 3F.

claim: NKX2.2 is an immunohistochemical marker that has been reported to be sensitive and specific for Ewing sarcoma in humans.
source: NKX2.2 is an immunohistochemical marker that has been reported to be sensitive and specific for Ewing sarcoma in human (McCuiston and Bishop, 2018).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1-expressing cells in zebrafish tumors are positive for nkx2.2a.
source: We found that consistent with human data the EWSR1-FLI1-expressing cells in tumor were also positive for nkx2.2a (Figure 3F, EWSR1-FLI).
evidence: This is experimental data from RNA scope staining shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Zebrafish embryos mosaically expressing EWSR1-FLI1 developed outgrowths visible as discrete cell masses.
source: Zebrafish embryos mosaically expressing EWSR1-FLI1, but not control embryos, developed outgrowths visible as discrete cell masses.
evidence: This is experimental data from imaging of embryos.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1-expressing outgrowths show increased cell proliferation as indicated by anti-phospho-histone H3 staining.
source: Immunostaining with anti-phospho-histone H3 (pH3) showed increased cell proliferation in these areas, associated with expression of EWSR1-FLI1 as indicated by the associated eGFP marker (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunostaining shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cells expressing EWSR1-FLI1 in zebrafish embryos are positive for pERK1/2.
source: Cells expressing EWSR1-FLI1 were positive for pERK1/2 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Most pERK1/2-positive cells in EWSR1-FLI1-expressing embryos also expressed EWSR1-FLI1.
source: While most pERK1/2-positive cells also expressed EWSR1-FLI1 (Figure 4C, Videos 1 and 2), some surrounding cells lacking the transgene were also marked with pH3 and pERK1/2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Some cells surrounding EWSR1-FLI1-expressing cells are positive for pH3 and pERK1/2 despite lacking the transgene.
source: While most pERK1/2-positive cells also expressed EWSR1-FLI1 (Figure 4C, Videos 1 and 2), some surrounding cells lacking the transgene were also marked with pH3 and pERK1/2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Activation of ERK1/2 signaling is an early event in EWSR1-FLI1-driven aberrations.
source: Thus, activation of ERK1/2 signaling is an early event in EWSR1-FLI1-driven aberrations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of pERK1/2 in early embryonic outgrowths.

claim: The GOBP_ERK1_AND_ERK2_CASCADE gene set is significantly enriched in zebrafish tumor proteomic dataset (NES:1.3867193, FWER p value: 0.03).
source: We found that the GOBP_ERK1_AND_ERK2_CASCADE gene set was significantly enriched in zebrafish tumor proteomic dataset (NES:1.3867193, FWER p value: 0.03) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is experimental data from GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: ERK1/2 is active in advanced zebrafish tumors.
source: Similar to EWSR1-FLI1-driven outgrowth in larvae, ERK1/2 is active in advanced zebrafish tumors.
evidence: This is experimental data from IHC and immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: ERK1/2 signaling activity in zebrafish tumors is heterogeneous, with focal areas showing more intense signaling activity.
source: ERK1/2 signaling activity in tumors was heterogeneous, with focal areas showing Video 1 more intense signaling activity.
evidence: This is experimental data from IHC analysis.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 significantly affects protein expression in zebrafish embryos.
source: EWSR1-FLI1 significantly affects protein expression in zebrafish embryos (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: 248 differentially expressed proteins were affected by EWSR1-FLI1 at 24 hpf.
source: We identified 248 differentially expressed proteins affected by EWSR1-FLI1 at 24 hpf, and 1102 at 48 hpf (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 1102 differentially expressed proteins were affected by EWSR1-FLI1 at 48 hpf.
source: We identified 248 differentially expressed proteins affected by EWSR1-FLI1 at 24 hpf, and 1102 at 48 hpf (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Downregulated proteins comprised 65% of differentially expressed proteins at 24 hpf.
source: Downregulated proteins comprised 65% and 73% of differentially expressed proteins at 24 and 48 hpf, respectively, suggesting that EWSR1-FLI1 was acting mostly as a transcriptional repressor rather than an activator (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Downregulated proteins comprised 73% of differentially expressed proteins at 48 hpf.
source: Downregulated proteins comprised 65% and 73% of differentially expressed proteins at 24 and 48 hpf, respectively, suggesting that EWSR1-FLI1 was acting mostly as a transcriptional repressor rather than an activator (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 acts mostly as a transcriptional repressor rather than an activator.
source: Downregulated proteins comprised 65% and 73% of differentially expressed proteins at 24 and 48 hpf, respectively, suggesting that EWSR1-FLI1 was acting mostly as a transcriptional repressor rather than an activator (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that most differentially expressed proteins are downregulated.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 expression is associated with upregulated expression of proteins involved in ECM reorganization, proteoglycan metabolism, and protein synthesis.
source: Importantly, we found a strong upregulation of proteins involved in extracellular matrix (ECM) reorganization, proteoglycan metabolism, and protein synthesis (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is experimental data from GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 expression in zebrafish embryos is associated with upregulated expression of collagens col1a1b, col1a2, col2a1a, col9a1b, col9a2, and col28a2a.
source: The proteomics data revealed that EWSR1-FLI1 expression in zebrafish embryos is associated with upregulated expression of collagens col1a1b, col1a2, col2a1a, col9a1b, col9a2, and col28a2a, which are involved in ECM organization and skeletal system development.
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis.

claim: Proteins involved in proteoglycan catabolism were significantly differentially expressed in embryos expressing EWSR1-FLI1.
source: Proteins involved in proteoglycan catabolism were also significantly differentially expressed in embryos expressing EWSR1-FLI1 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase (sgsh) is upregulated in embryos expressing EWSR1-FLI1.
source: Among the top identified hits was N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase (sgsh), the enzyme involved in heparan sulfate proteoglycan catabolism (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: gnsb and gnsa (N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase) enzymes involved in hydrolysis of heparan sulfate chains are upregulated in embryos expressing EWSR1-FLI1.
source: We also found upregulated gnsb and gnsa (N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase) enzymes involved in hydrolysis of heparan sulfate chains.
evidence: This is experimental data from LC-MS/MS analysis.

claim: Expression of enzymes involved in proteoglycan metabolism is strongly upregulated in human Ewing sarcoma tumor samples compared to normal tissue.
source: Expression of enzymes involved in proteoglycan metabolism was strongly upregulated in tumor samples compared to normal tissue (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is data from analysis of human microarray data (GSE17674) shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Enzymes involved in the catabolism of heparan sulfate proteoglycans (including SGSH, GNS, HS3ST4, HS3ST1, HS2ST1, and HS6ST1) are upregulated in human Ewing sarcoma.
source: Specifically, we found upregulation of enzymes involved in the catabolism of heparan sulfate proteoglycans (including SGSH, GNS, HS3ST4, HS3ST1, HS2ST1, and HS6ST1) in human Ewing sarcoma (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is data from analysis of human microarray data (GSE17674) shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Surfen is a sulfated heparan sulfate antagonist with a high affinity to all sulfated GAGs.
source: Surfen is a sulfated heparan sulfate antagonist with a high affinity to all sulfated GAGs (Schuksz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about surfen supported by citation.

claim: Surfen blocks sulfation and degradation of GAG chains in vitro.
source: Surfen blocks sulfation and degradation of GAG chains in vitro and affects growth factor binding and proteoglycan-mediated signal transduction through certain cell surface growth factor receptors (Schuksz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about surfen supported by citation.

claim: Surfen affects growth factor binding and proteoglycan-mediated signal transduction through certain cell surface growth factor receptors.
source: Surfen blocks sulfation and degradation of GAG chains in vitro and affects growth factor binding and proteoglycan-mediated signal transduction through certain cell surface growth factor receptors (Schuksz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about surfen supported by citation.

claim: Addition of 5 or 10 μM surfen strongly significantly inhibited ERK1/2 phosphorylation in TC32 and EWS502 cells.
source: Addition of 5 or 10 μM surfen strongly significantly inhibited ERK1/2 phosphorylation (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: This is experimental data from immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: Blocking proteoglycan metabolism impairs ERK1/2 signaling in Ewing sarcoma cells.
source: Thus, blocking proteoglycan metabolism impairs ERK1/2 signaling in Ewing sarcoma cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that surfen (which blocks proteoglycan metabolism) reduces ERK1/2 phosphorylation.

claim: Treatment with surfen significantly reduces the proliferation rates of TC32 and EWS502 Ewing sarcoma cells.
source: Treatment with surfen significantly reduces the proliferation rates of Ewing sarcoma cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is experimental data from proliferation assays shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Treatment of TC32 cells with 10 μM surfen resulted in a 62.7% decrease in proliferation compared to control cells.
source: Importantly, treatment of cells with surfen at 10 μM resulted in a decrease of TC32 proliferation by 62.7%, and EWS502 by 63.4% compared to control cells treated with 0.2% DMSO (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is experimental data from proliferation assays shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Treatment of EWS502 cells with 10 μM surfen resulted in a 63.4% decrease in proliferation compared to control cells.
source: Importantly, treatment of cells with surfen at 10 μM resulted in a decrease of TC32 proliferation by 62.7%, and EWS502 by 63.4% compared to control cells treated with 0.2% DMSO (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is experimental data from proliferation assays shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Surfen treatment caused morphological changes in TC32 and EWS502 cells.
source: Surfen treatment caused morphological changes in TC32 and EWS502 cells (Figure 6D), consistent with predicted effects on cell adhesion.
evidence: This is experimental data from imaging shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Treatment of cells with surfen led to a significant reduction in colony number for both TC32 and EWS502 cell lines.
source: Treatment of cells with surfen led to a significant reduction in colony number for both cell lines (Figure 6, F).
evidence: This is experimental data from clonogenic assays shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Treatment of TC32 cells with 2.5 μM surfen led to a 90.3% decrease in colony number.
source: More specifically, the treatment of TC32 cell with 2.5 μM surfen led to a 90.3% decrease of colony number while treatment of EWS502 cells with 2.5 μM surfen resulted in a 97.8% decrease of colony forming units.
evidence: This is experimental data from clonogenic assays.

claim: Treatment of EWS502 cells with 2.5 μM surfen resulted in a 97.8% decrease in colony forming units.
source: More specifically, the treatment of TC32 cell with 2.5 μM surfen led to a 90.3% decrease of colony number while treatment of EWS502 cells with 2.5 μM surfen resulted in a 97.8% decrease of colony forming units.
evidence: This is experimental data from clonogenic assays.

claim: Surfen inhibited outgrowth development in the zebrafish embryo model of Ewing sarcoma.
source: Consistent with results on human cells, surfen inhibited outgrowth development in the zebrafish embryo model of Ewing sarcoma.
evidence: This is experimental data from zebrafish treatment experiments shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Treatment of embryos with 1 μM trametinib or 0.2 μM surfen has comparable effects on outgrowth formation.
source: We found that treatment of outgrowths with 1 μM trametinib or 0.2 μM surfen has comparable effects on outgrowth formation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is experimental data from zebrafish treatment experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Surfen treatment of fish expressing EWSR1-FLI1 resulted in significant rescue of the fin phenotype.

claim: Surfen significantly reduced tumor size by 30% during the first 15 days in zebrafish with established tumors.
source: We found that surfen significantly reduced the tumor size by 30% during the first 15 days while tumors treated with DMSO showed increase in tumor size by 46% (Figure 7B, C; Figure 7—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is experimental data from zebrafish tumor treatment experiments shown in Figure 7B and 7C.

claim: Tumors treated with DMSO showed increase in tumor size by 46% over 15 days.
source: We found that surfen significantly reduced the tumor size by 30% during the first 15 days while tumors treated with DMSO showed increase in tumor size by 46% (Figure 7B, C; Figure 7—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is experimental data from zebrafish tumor treatment experiments shown in Figure 7B and 7C.

claim: Surfen is effective both preventing the outgrowth formation in embryonic model of Ewing sarcoma and tumor progression in older fish.
source: Based on that we conclude that surfen is effective both preventing the outgrowth formation in embryonic model of Ewing sarcoma and tumor progression in older fish.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data showing surfen's effects in both embryonic and adult zebrafish models.

claim: Fewer than 30% of Ewing sarcoma patients presenting with metastases survive for 5 years.

source: The importance of tumor microenvironment and communication between cancerous and host cells has become evident as essential for tumor formation and invasion.
evidence: This is established knowledge in cancer biology.

source: Cre-inducible expression of EWSR1-FLI1 under cmv and b-actin ubiquitous promoters did not result in a high incidence of tumor development.

source: The pattern of Cre-induced eGFP-2A-EWSR1-FLI1 expression was consistently different from Cre-induced eGFP expression driven by the same ubiquitin promoter (Figure 3B), suggesting that EWSR1-FLI1 can be tolerated by certain cell types while being toxic for others.

claim: EWSR1-FLI1 can be tolerated by certain cell types while being toxic for others.

claim: Human Ewing sarcoma can occur in any part of the body in bone or soft tissue.
source: Human Ewing sarcoma can occur in any part of the body in bone or soft tissue.

evidence: This is established knowledge from previous research supported by citation.
